incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20 (SAS provisions), and Règlement général du Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) within the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) and the M0 form (Déclaration de création d'entreprise)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; however, if share capital is set below €50,000, it must be fully paid up at incorporation. For capital ≥€50,000, at least 50% of cash contributions must be paid up at incorporation, with the remainder within 5 years. Capital must be deposited in a blocked bank account or with a notary until registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shareholders of the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) hereby subscribe to the share capital as set forth in the Articles of Association, and that the initial capital contributions be deposited in accordance with law. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [address], France, and that the President be appointed as legal representative. RESOLVED, that the President is authorized to execute all documents and filings necessary for incorporation, including the publication of the legal notice and registration with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce. RESOLVED, that the corporate seal be adopted and the bank account be opened.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (optional but recommended) or all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Statuts in French, including corporate name, registered office address, share capital, share classes, governance rules, and the appointment of the President. All shareholders must sign the document. If capital is in cash, deposit the funds with a bank or notary and obtain a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds).
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Statuts are incomplete or non-compliant, the registry will issue a query; correct and resubmit within 15 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish a Legal Notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized legal gazette (e.g., Les Affiches Parisiennes, Le Bulletin Officiel des Annonces Civiles et Commerciales)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish a notice containing the company name, legal form (SAS), share capital, registered office address, purpose, and the identity of the President. Obtain a certificate of publication (attestation de parution).
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice is incomplete, the gazette will request corrections; re-submit with amendments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Incorporation Dossier with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Commercial Court Registry) of the registered office's jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed M0 form, the signed Statuts, the certificate of publication, the capital deposit certificate (if applicable), and identification documents of the President and shareholders. Pay the filing fee. The registry will review and issue a K-bis extract upon approval.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office address (e.g., lease agreement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the dossier is incomplete, the registry will issue a 'demande de régularisation' (request for regularization); provide missing documents within 30 days to avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the K-bis Extract and Post-Incorporation Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, the registry issues the K-bis extract, which serves as the official proof of incorporation. Subsequently, register for social security (URSSAF), obtain a SIRET number, and open a corporate bank account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the K-bis is delayed, contact the registry; if errors are found, request a correction.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction Régionale de l'Économie, de l'Emploi, du Travail et des Solidarités (DREETS) – for workplace compliance; no specific industrial license required for LED fixture assembly
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable – activity is not subject to a specific operating license under French law

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – activity falls under the 'rubrique 2740' of the ICPE (Installations Classées pour la Protection de l'Environnement) but is below the threshold requiring a declaration or authorization
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EU Directive 2011/65/EU (RoHS) and 2012/19/EU (WEEE) for hazardous substances and waste; wastewater discharge must meet local municipal limits; VOC emissions from soldering processes must comply with Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions) if applicable, but typically below thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire department (SDIS) for the premises, structural load inspection for any mezzanine or heavy equipment, and workplace clearance from the DREETS for compliance with the Labor Code (Code du travail) regarding safety and health.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle et numérique; e-filing portal: impots.gouv.fr (Espace Professionnel); single business registration portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; e-invoicing platform: Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) operated by the Agence pour l'Informatique Financière de l'État (AIFE) under DGFiP; dedicated unit for foreign taxpayers: Service des Impôts des Entreprises Étrangères (SIEE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly constituted SAS, incorporation is filed through the Guichet des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); DGFiP and the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés automatically assign the corporate TIN comprising a 9-digit SIREN, one or more SIRET site numbers and, upon VAT registration, the French intra-community VAT number (format: FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN). Foreign-controlled SAS shareholders and non-resident directors are permitted; K-bis extract evidences registration. For a foreign company selling into France without a French establishment, direct VAT registration is obtained via the SIEE procedure: file the SIEE application form with certificate of incorporation, proof of home-country tax/VAT status, director identity documents, and, where required, a fiscal representative mandate; the SIEE issues a French intra-community VAT number. A resident SAS is mandatorily within the corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés / IS) net; its first accounting period and corporate tax return (déclaration de résultats) are due within 60 days of legal registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Impôt sur les Sociétés / IS) — mandatory for the SAS; standard IS rate 25% for fiscal year 2025, with a reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit for SMEs satisfying Article 219 CGI conditions (turnover below EUR 10 million, fully paid-up capital, at least 75% held directly or indirectly by individual shareholders); territorial scope under Article 209 I CGI: a French-domiciled SAS is taxable in France on profits from French operations; income of foreign permanent establishments is taxable only if the company elects worldwide or per-country net income treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France applies no US-style check-the-box regime; the SAS is a non-transparent entity and IS liability is statutory. Available elections: (i) the 'bénéfice net mondial' or 'bénéfice net par pays' option to include foreign branch profits on a worldwide or per-country net basis (Article 209 I CGI); (ii) election for fiscal integration (régime d'intégration fiscale, Article 223 A et seq. CGI) for a French parent holding at least 95% of French subsidiaries; (iii) claim of the 15% reduced IS rate for qualifying SMEs; (iv) VAT small-business franchise (franchise en base de TVA) below statutory thresholds. Anti-hybrid rules implementing ATAD (Articles 212 bis, 212 bis A, 209 VII CGI) apply mandatorily; no elective hybrid mismatch regime exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) — Value Added Tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual taxable turnover for supplies of goods, with EUR 93,500 tolerance limit; EUR 37,500 for services, with EUR 41,250 tolerance limit, pursuant to Loi de finances 2024. A manufacturing SAS selling commercial LED grow light fixtures is a goods supplier; VAT registration is mandatory once turnover exceeds the EUR 85,000 main threshold, and exporters are typically registered from inception in order to recover input VAT and substantiate 0% export treatment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory structured e-invoicing under Articles 289 bis and 289 ter CGI as amended by the Loi de finances pour 2025: from 1 September 2026 all taxable persons must be capable of receiving standardized e-invoices through the PPF or certified Partner Dematerialization Platforms (PDPs), and large enterprises and intermediate-sized enterprises (ETIs) must issue e-invoices; from 1 September 2027 small and micro enterprises (PME/TPE) must issue e-invoices. The regime is a transactional data transmission model using API-based routing from certified PDPs to the PPF; it is not a real-time fiscal pre-clearance or digital stamping system. Mandatory data formats are Factur-X (hybrid), UBL 2.3 and UN/CEFACT CII. The separately planned e-reporting obligation was abandoned by the 2025 Finance Act; intra-community recapitulative statements (DEB/DES) remain obligatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union qualify for the export exemption (economic equivalent of zero-rating) under Article 262 et seq. CGI. Conditions: (i) the seller as exporter holds an accepted customs export declaration (DELTA electronic filing, DAU-H15); (ii) goods must genuinely leave EU territory, with administrative doctrine on the BOI-TVA-CHAMP-30-30-20 series requiring dispatch/export completion within 90 days of delivery; (iii) transport documentation (B/L, CMR international, air waybill) is issued in the exporter's name or on its behalf; (iv) the transaction is supported by commercial invoicing and payment evidence. B2B supplies to EU VAT-registered customers are likewise exempt (Article 262 ter I CGI) when the customer's valid French/EU VAT number is obtained and reported on the recapitulative statement. Manufactured horticultural LED grow light fixtures delivered on DDP/DAP Incoterms to non-EU buyers are within the exemption if the documentary chain is complete. French input VAT is recovered through the periodic CA3 return (régime réel normal), or, for non-established foreign taxable persons, under Directive 2008/9/EC via the French electronic refund portal within statutory deadlines.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU-H15 / DELTA electronic acceptance proof)
Bill of Lading (B/L), multimodal transport document, CMR international consignment note or air waybill proving dispatch to the non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transaction evidence showing settlement and repatriation of the export receivable
Commercial invoice and packing list issued in the exporter's name
Evidence of transport contract and cargo insurance, preferably aligning with DDP/DAP Incoterms
K-bis extraction and valid French intra-community VAT number evidence of the exporting SAS
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP auditors apply the BOI-TVA-CHAMP-30-30-20 documentation doctrine in export reviews; any missing, inconsistent or false document, or proof that goods did not leave EU territory within the admitted 90-day export window, triggers restoration of French VAT on the gross export price. Restoration is accompanied by late-payment interest at 0.20% per month (2.4% per annum) plus a 40% penalty for deliberate under-declaration (Article 1729 CGI) or an 80% penalty for fraudulent manoeuvres or abusive tax avoidance, including via the abuse-of-right procedure. Export proceeds are further subject to French financial relations regulations requiring timely repatriation of receivables from non-EU counterparties; the 180-day period stated in this dossier is the administrative baseline customarily applied in French transfer-pricing and FX repatriation compliance policies, and non-compliance may trigger Article 1649 quinquies B bis CGI reporting sanctions and, in aggravated customs fraud cases, customs penalties under Title XII of the Code des Douanes of up to three times the evaded duties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting together with the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) as licensing and supervisory arm and the Direction Générale du Trésor for external financial policy and EU restrictive measures; the legal framework is the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) as harmonised with EU law.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France observes complete liberalisation of current and capital account transactions for EEA countries and most third countries under Article 63 TFEU, subject to EU sanctions and counter-proliferation controls. Non-resident shareholders of a French SAS may freely contribute equity, subscribe capital, receive dividends, liquidation proceeds, and repay shareholder loans without FX authorization or surrender. A French bank must establish a Banque de France external-payments reporting category and may require documentary evidence of the underlying capital movement. De facto friction is limited to enhanced KYC/CDD, sanctions screening, source-of-funds proof, and bank risk appetite; no legal limit or central-bank licence applies to profit remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or conversion obligation applies to French exporters. Export proceeds may be held indefinitely in euros or foreign currency and may be used for any lawful purpose. The only mandatory elements are reporting obligations: goods exports are captured by customs declarations; financial flows and related direct investment positions are recorded through Banque de France balance-of-payments reporting when thresholds are met; all payments must be made via a bank or authorised payment institution. There are no statutory surrender deadlines, minimum conversion percentages, or dedicated proceeds accounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (Crédit Agricole CIB)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Cash Management and Trade Finance Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI and B2B payment platforms, including Airwallex and equivalent EU-authorised EMI passported into France under PSD2, are viable as secondary operational rails for euro-US-dollar and euro-CNY payments, supplier settlements, and low-to-mid-value disbursements; viability is High for ordinary trade flows but Low-Medium for capital-escrow and high-value treasury functions. Legal constraints: an EMI cannot take deposits, cannot grant or administrate proprietary credit on its own books, must safeguard client monies, must operate through a French-registered or registered-branch service, and must comply with ACPR/Orias registration and AML/CTF rules. An EMI-issued IBAN is not universally accepted by French customs or some counterparty banks for LC/demand-guarantee transactions; the primary treasury account should remain with a credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not categorically mandate physical presence for KYC interviews if the bank applies secure remote identification (video verification with NFC passport chip or an ACPR-recognised digital identity provider). In practice, tier-1 commercial banks usually require at least one in-person or notarized meeting for all non-resident UBOs and legal representatives before opening a capital-escrow account, and may require a French registered office/domiciliation agent for the SAS. Remote opening is possible for EU/EEA passport-holding principals and simple ownership structures; the bank's risk appetite, not the statute, is the controlling factor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: the SAS's equity is held by a foreign intermediate holding company with ultimate natural persons outside the EU/EEA and not visible in French or ORBIS registries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Kbis extract, the RBE (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) filing receipt, certified group organisational chart, constitutional documents of every holding entity, share ledger, passport copies plus proof of residential address for each natural-person UBO, and a formal legal-opinion letter confirming the ownership chain from qualified counsel in the UBO's jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party funding: an inbound investment or capital increase is settled not by the nominal shareholder but by another related or group treasury company, triggering circular or undisclosed-source concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the SAS annual general meeting/shareholder resolution authorising the capital contribution, the exact SWIFT remitter identity matching the shareholder's KYC file, a declared payment purpose code of direct investment/capital contribution, consolidated audited group financial statements proving available liquidity, intercompany loan or settlement agreements if applicable, and a signed source-of-funds declaration with bank statements from the remitting entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic-purpose mismatch: a small capital SAS declaring high-value LED grow-light trade with overseas affiliated companies without clear physical activity or inventory.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit advance-pricing or transfer-pricing policy, signed commercial agreements, warehouse/logistics contracts, purchase orders and pro-forma invoices, HS/ISIC descriptor references, CE/RoHS/relevant product compliance certificates, planned staffing and premises lease, and a credible twelve-month cash-flow forecast with ledger mapping to the ISIC 2740 horticultural LED scope.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/high-risk jurisdiction nexus: counterparties or ultimate suppliers located in jurisdictions subject to restrictive measures or grey-list AML risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an independent sanctions and adverse-media report covering UBOs, counterparties, and supply-chain red flags; jurisdictions such as FATF monitoree/countries requiring enhanced due diligence; end-user undertakings or final-destination declarations; transactional-level compliance mapping showing no OSC/FATF prohibited exposure; and the bank's qualified-compliance response memorandum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Abnormal FX velocity: treasury activities include frequent forward conversions with no apparent commercial basis or low-margin circular payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the treasury policy, each underlying trade invoice and settlement instruction, bank-form hedge ticket marked 'hedge of a genuine commercial exposure', transactional history reconciling FX use with sales/purchase terms, and a written authorisation by the SAS president/director defining treasury approval limits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103/TT or ISO 20022 equivalent via a French-authorised credit institution, with the remitter name exactly matching the registered shareholder and the beneficiary exactly matching the SAS's KYC file. The message must include a capital-contribution/direct-investment purpose code and clear remark text such as 'SAS capital increase / contribution to share capital under L.227-1 et seq. of the French Commercial Code'; include a copy of the shareholders' resolution and bank certificate in the payment file if requested. For amounts above the applicable Banque de France external-reporting thresholds, the bank will classify the flow as direct investment for balance-of-payments/statistical reporting. Same-currency, same-name, pre-advised transfers avoid rejected wires and create a clean audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier settlements: standard SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers from the SAS euro account or EMI rail, using trade invoice references and appropriate HS codes; for larger or document-backed transactions with non-EU counterparties: documentary irrevocable commercial letters of credit opened through a French bank in EUR/USD/CNY under UCP600, with complying presentation of invoice, bill of lading/airway bill, certificate of origin, and insurance; for SEPA/EUR disbursements in the EU: instant SEPA CT and SEPA Direct Debit for low-risk recurring payments.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forwards entered with a French credit institution or EU-authorised investment firm solely to hedge forecast transactional EUR/USD or EUR/CNY exposure.
Cross-currency swaps (Basis swaps / FX swaps) for financing and balance-sheet hedging where the matching borrowing or trade payable is specifically documented.
FX options and option strategies (call/put collars) with a MiFID-licensed counterparty, subject to professional/eligible-counterparty status and EMIR clearing/reporting thresholds.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for emerging-market currencies lacking deliverable legal tender; NDFs are unnecessary for major convertible currencies and may be disallowed if used speculatively.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry (Greffe) through the INPI single filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must be approved within six months after the financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court injunction and potential daily penalty; monetary fine generally EUR 1,500, increasing to EUR 3,000 for repeat non-compliance. No automatic strike-off occurs solely because annual accounts are late.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and annexes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a financial year ending on 31 December, generally by the second business day after 1 May of the following year; other year-ends generally within three months after year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may trigger a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest generally at 0.20% per month, and higher penalties for deliberate or fraudulent conduct.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises (CFE) annual tax payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally payable by 15 December each year; a 50% advance payment is generally due by 15 June where the applicable threshold is met.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment may result in a 5% surcharge and late-payment interest; the tax amount is assessed by reference to the company's French premises and local tax rates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the INPI single filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual confirmation filing is required. Changes to beneficial ownership or control must generally be reported within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate information may result in judicial orders, fines, and restrictions affecting registration compliance. No automatic annual strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate officer and registered-office information update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Court Registry through the INPI single filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven filing, generally within one month after a change in the registered office, legal representative, company name, activity, or other registered particulars.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to update the RCS may cause registry discrepancies, court injunctions, and fines; administrative removal is not triggered automatically by a single late update.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor is generally mandatory for an SAS exceeding at least two of the following thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million total balance sheet, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Appointment may also be required for certain controlled or controlling groups, or by court order or shareholder request.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Authority (ANC) regulations applies to statutory individual accounts. IFRS may be used for qualifying consolidated accounts and where legally permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require an annual beneficial-owner confirmation solely because a new year begins. The SAS must maintain shareholder account records and a share-transfer register, record transfers promptly, and file an updated beneficial-owner declaration within the applicable period when ownership or control changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Shareholder account ledger and share-transfer register
Register or book of corporate decisions and shareholder resolutions
Corporate officer, registered-office, and beneficial-owner records supporting current RCS and beneficial-owner filings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 325-1,625 per year for commercial domiciliation or registered-office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 2,000-10,000 per year, depending on transaction volume, group structure, accounting quality, and audit scope

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard French corporate income tax 'impôt sur les sociétés' – IS – for fiscal years opened on or after 1 January 2022; reduced 15% rate applies to the first €42,500 of taxable profit for small companies below the SME thresholds).
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on first €42,500 of profit if turnover < €10M (Art. 219 CGI); R&D tax credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D costs up to €100M (Art. 244 quater B); Innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% for SME prototypes; 10% reduced rate on net patent/industrial-property royalties (Art. 39 terdecies); JEI full/partial IS exemption for young innovative companies in first 7 years (Art. 44 sexies-0 A); all capped by the EU/State aid GBER.
stage_6.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward ('report en avant'), but the annual offset of the carried-forward loss is capped at €1,000,000 plus 50% of the taxable profit exceeding €1,000,000 (Art. 209 CGI). Optional carryback ('report en arrière') is limited to the immediately preceding profitable financial year, with the resulting tax credit usable/refundable over 5 years (Art. 220 quinquies CGI).
